title: Edge-Deployed Reasoning for Field Diagnostics
business: Remote industrial maintenance teams operating in disconnected environments.
problem: Field technicians require high-reasoning diagnostic support for complex machinery but lack high-bandwidth connectivity to cloud-based LLMs and cannot fit 54GB FP16 models on ruggedized edge hardware.
solution: Deploying the Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf model allows technicians to run a 27B-class reasoning engine locally on portable hardware. By utilizing the PTQ1_0 ternary packing format, the model footprint is reduced to approximately 5.95 GB, enabling full diagnostic capabilities without cloud dependency.
steps: Clone the specialized PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp fork to ensure compatibility with ternary hybrid-attention kernels.
Compile the llama.cpp binary with appropriate hardware flags (CUDA for GPU-equipped rugged tablets or Metal for Apple Silicon).
Download the Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf file to the local storage of the field device.
Configure the inference engine to use xhigh reasoning effort for complex diagnostic chains.
Execute the model via the llama-cli using the recommended sampling parameters (temperature 1.0, min_p 0.05).
outcome: Technicians achieve autonomous, high-quality diagnostic reasoning in the field, reducing machine downtime by eliminating the need for cloud round-trips.
limitation: The model requires a specific llama.cpp fork; using stock versions will cause the runtime to reject the ternary weights or produce corrupted output. Verification is performed by checking that the binary correctly loads the Hadamard rotation metadata.

code.content:
# Run inference using the PTQ1_0 packed model on edge hardware
./bin/llama-cli -m Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -fa on -c 32768 \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.05 \
  -p "Analyze turbine vibration error code 402." -n 16384
code.explanation: This command executes the model locally, utilizing the ternary kernels to process diagnostic queries within the memory constraints of a field device.
